title: Reversible whole-body cryopreservation of adult mice

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 2, Cryopreservation. Target: reversibly cryopreserve and recover live, intact wild-type adult mice whole-body, frozen or vitrified for at least 24 hours, with more than 99% viability and no permanent organ damage, under ethics approval. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BIO on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Reversible whole-body cryopreservation of adult mice
page.definition: Adult wild-type mice—mice without inherited genetic modifications—can return alive from whole-body freezing or vitrification, solidification into an ice-free glass. Preservation lasts at least 24 hours, recovery exceeds 99% viability, and no permanent organ damage or bodily harm occurs.

goal.need: Isolated rat kidneys have been preserved at −150 °C for up to 100 days and subsequently supported transplant recipients. Whole-body recovery requires preservation of the coordinated function of organs and brain together. Advanced Neural Biosciences identifies simultaneous preservation of transplant organs as an application of whole-body vitrification.

statements.quote: recover live wild-type mice with high viability.
statements.context: The stated objective of Problem 02, Cryopreservation, in The Millennium Problems for Biology.

statements.body: Advanced Neural Biosciences, in the CryoDAO-funded CRYORAT programme
statements.quote: Whole-body vitrification would also permit in-situ multi-organ preservation for organ transplantation.

completion.title: Adult wild-type mice recover after ≥24 hours frozen or vitrified, with >99% viability and no permanent harm.
completion.criterion: Live, intact, wild-type adult mice undergo whole-body freezing or vitrification for at least 24 hours and recover with >99% viability, without permanent organ damage or bodily harm. Experiments require ethics approval. Somatic genetic engineering is permitted but discouraged. The challenge specifies no cohort size, viability assay, statistical confidence requirement, follow-up duration or organ-injury acceptance tests.
completion.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, The Millennium Problems for Biology, Problem 02: Cryopreservation; published research-challenge conditions.
completion.threshold_quote: The mice must remain frozen or vitrified for at least 24 hours, must be recovered with >99% viability,
completion.basis: The published challenge directly specifies the animal, whole-body preservation state, minimum storage duration, recovery fraction, absence of permanent harm and ethics approval. These conditions match the capability. Its undefined viability and injury assessments prevent fully specified adjudication without additional conditions from the challenge's authors.

milestones.title: Vitrified adult mouse brain slices recover synaptic transmission and long-term potentiation.
milestones.criterion: Rewarmed adult mouse hippocampal slices recover evoked synaptic responses and long-term potentiation, a lasting increase in synaptic strength. Published on 3 March 2026, German et al. measured potentiation at 138.06 ± 6.90% of baseline in 7 vitrified slices from 7 mice, versus 157.68 ± 7.14% in 8 control slices from 7 mice, 51–60 minutes after stimulation. This establishes tissue function; it does not establish retention of previously learned information.
milestones.set_by: Functional electrophysiology convention described in McKenzie et al.'s biostasis research roadmap, section 6, and applied by German et al., Figure 2.
milestones.threshold_quote: a long-term potentiation (LTP) response in vitrified and rewarmed hippocampal slices

milestones.title: A vitrified kidney sustains a rat without native kidneys for 30 days after transplantation.
milestones.criterion: After vitrification, storage, rewarming and transplantation, the preserved kidney provides the recipient's sole renal support through the published 30-day endpoint. Han et al., published on 9 June 2023, achieved 30-day survival in all 5 recipients of vitrified and rewarmed kidneys, alongside 5 fresh-kidney controls. Preserved grafts initially showed dysfunction for 2–3 weeks before renal function normalized.
milestones.set_by: Han et al., published rat-kidney transplantation protocol and 30-day experimental endpoint; this endpoint was established for isolated rat kidneys.
milestones.threshold_quote: Nanowarmed organs restored renal function and solely sustained the lives of nephrectomized transplant recipients for 30 days post transplant.

milestones.title: A cryopreserved mammalian brain recovers integrated function after rewarming and blood reperfusion.
milestones.criterion: Recover function of the whole brain after cryopreservation, rewarming, removal of protective chemicals and reperfusion with warm oxygenated blood. Assess integrated function through electrical activity, metabolism and, where applicable, behavior. The roadmap supplies no numerical acceptance limits. German et al. recovered hippocampal slice function after in-situ brain storage at −140 °C for 1–8 days; one in three protocol iterations yielded usable tissue. Those measurements did not establish integrated whole-brain recovery.
milestones.set_by: McKenzie et al., Biostasis: A Roadmap for Research in Preservation and Potential Revival of Humans, section 6; published whole-brain reversibility assay.
milestones.threshold_quote: reperfusion of the whole brain with warm, oxygenated blood

milestones.title: Multiple organs retain viability after cryopreservation through a whole-body procedure.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate post-cryopreservation viability in multiple organs preserved through whole-body cryopreservation. CRYORAT specifies neither a minimum viability fraction nor storage temperature, duration or organ panel for this milestone. Its update of 13 January 2026 reports development of assays across multiple organs, without quantitative post-cryopreservation results or sample sizes; this programme update is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Advanced Neural Biosciences and CryoDAO, CRYORAT project, milestone 4; the published milestone concerns rats.
milestones.threshold_quote: Results that multiple organs can be cryopreserved with good viability through whole-body cryopreservation.

milestones.title: An intact adult wild-type mouse survives recovery after at least 24 hours frozen or vitrified.
milestones.criterion: Recover a living, intact wild-type adult mouse after at least 24 hours of whole-body freezing or vitrification in an ethics-approved experiment. This first whole-animal recovery precedes establishing the completion target's >99% viability and absence of permanent harm. No additional recovery fraction or follow-up interval is assigned.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback. Searches of the Millennium Problems challenge, CRYORAT programme, biostasis roadmap and primary mouse literature found no separately defined adult-mouse first-recovery milestone. This uses the challenge's animal and minimum storage duration, with live recovery as the narrowest intermediate result.

not_found: No adjudication supplement defining viability, sample size, follow-up or permanent injury for Problem 02 was found.
No published report of live recovery of an intact wild-type adult mouse after at least 24 hours of whole-body freezing or vitrification was found.

results.finding: Vitrified adult mouse hippocampal slices (7 slices from 7 mice) recovered long-term potentiation to 138.06 ± 6.90% of baseline.
results.detail: Evoked synaptic responses also recovered. In 8 control slices from 7 mice, potentiation was 157.68 ± 7.14% of baseline. The result does not establish retention of previously learned information.
results.quote: SC-CA1 LTP amounted to 157.68 ± 7.14 % in control slices (n = 8 from 7 mice), which was not significantly different from the extent of LTP in postvitrification slices (138.06 ± 6.90 %, n = 7 from 7 mice;

results.finding: All 5 rats receiving vitrified and rewarmed kidneys survived 30 days without native kidneys.
results.detail: Kidneys were stored for 1–100 days before transplantation. Graft function was initially impaired, with creatinine returning to control levels over 2–3 weeks.
results.quote: Postoperatively, all fresh control and nanowarmed kidney transplants continued to produce urine, and all animals survived for the full 30-day study period.
